card werk-test-fake-launch-log  [decided]
Each launch of the fake agent records the arguments it was given
why: A test must check what werk asked the agent, not only what the agent answered.

Each time werk starts the fake agent, the fake records the arguments of that launch in the temporary project. A test reads the record to check that werk started the agent with the right request.

  -> refines         werk-v0-seams-fake-script  The fake agent replays a script of ordered steps: an event to print, or a file to write
  -> depends_on      werk-base-test-project  Each werk test runs on a fresh project directory with an empty map
       why: The record lives in the fresh project of the test, so no other test reads it.

It means this: do not keep `#werk-fake-launch-role` as its own card. Add its one new fact to the decided card that already describes the launch record.

`#werk-test-fake-launch-log` says now:
> Each launch of the fake agent records **the arguments** it was given.

The ghost adds only one fact: the record also holds **the role name**. werk passes the role in the environment, not in the arguments. Everything else in the ghost repeats `#werk-test-fake-launch-log`. Two cards that describe one record can drift apart.

The staged change to `#werk-test-fake-launch-log` would be:
- **Title:** "Each launch of the fake agent records its arguments and its role"
- **Body:** "...the fake records the arguments of that launch and the role name from its environment (see #st-build-seam-role-env). A test reads the record to check that werk started each kind of agent with the right role and the right request."
- **New link:** `depends_on #st-build-seam-role-env`, because the role comes from that card.

The code in `werk-v0` already writes the role into the record. Then you discard the ghost.

Next: say "stage it" and I write the proposal on `#werk-test-fake-launch-log` for your ✓.

werk-test-fake-launch-log: proposed

Each time werk starts the fake agent, the fake records the arguments of that launch ==and the role name from its environment (see #st-build-seam-role-env)== in the temporary project. A test reads the record to check that werk started ==~~the~~ each kind of== agent with the right ==role and the right== request.
werk-test-fake-launch-log --depends_on--> st-build-seam-role-env
  why: takes the rule that each agent's role travels in its launch environment, which the record copies

I staged a change on `#werk-test-fake-launch-log`. It waits for your ✓.

- **Title:** "Each launch of the fake agent records its arguments and its role"
- **Why:** the role travels in the environment, not in the arguments, so the record holds both.
- **Body:** it adds the role, with "see #st-build-seam-role-env".

The new `depends_on` edge to `#st-build-seam-role-env` is already live. A staged change cannot hold an edge. `#st-build-seam-role-env` is decided and not stale. If you discard the change, I remove the edge.

After your ✓, press ✕ on the ghost `#werk-fake-launch-role`.
